- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > -0.22 over recent days), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 3–5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast tail (last 5–7 days).
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overestimate volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–15% relative to historical 18-day std.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward momentum in bearish sentiment; add 2–3% downward adjustment if sentiment < 0.05 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.22 to +0.17 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
